myth: When a boat did not come home, the women of the cliff set Tessal on the hearth, filled it with sea-water, and waited. Nobody sat by it. You do not sit beside a kettle for a drowned man; you put it on and get on with your mending. When Aun cut the string, the wind carried Tessal down the Leeward side, where the lamps are low, and it hangs there now with its spout turned toward home. Kael casts past it every night and hauls up only steam, and grumbles. Hesk counts it each turn of the Reel and has never once seen it boil. That is the way of it. If it boils, the one out there is climbing the cliff path with wet boots and an empty belly, and someone had better have the tea ready. So keep the kettle full, child, and keep your hands busy.
verse:
Set the kettle on
for the one still out past the sky
it will never boil
